title: Set a differential angle while keeping its floating output centred
instruction: Set the differential bar to the green angle band while keeping its central carriage on the white centre band throughout the adjustment. Move only the two blue input handles. Do not touch the output bar or its central carriage. Release both handles when done. The trainer is unpowered.
context: Two controls can share an output that must remain fixed during an adjustment. Moving one control and correcting the other later is insufficient. This contact driven trainer tests continuous coordination of both arms while changing the differential angle.
setup: Use the official bimanual YAM station. The tabletop is at z 747.5 mm. x points forward. y points left. z points up. Bolt the three guide bases to the table. The output root is at x 240 mm and y 0 mm on the tabletop. Its carriage has a passive y stroke from negative 50 mm to positive 50 mm. The carriage is a 25 mm by 25 mm by 20 mm block of mass 40 g. Its centre starts 35 mm above the table. The orange bar is 160 mm by 10 mm by 10 mm with mass 60 g. Its centre starts 45 mm above the table. It pivots about z on the carriage with limits negative 35 degrees and positive 35 degrees. Both input roots are at y 0 mm with x 305 mm and 175 mm. Each blue fork has mass 55 g and moves along y through negative 45 mm to positive 45 mm. Each fork has two 10 mm by 6 mm by 16 mm contact walls. Their local y centres are negative 12 mm and positive 12 mm. Their centres start 45 mm above the table. A lower bridge and an upper bridge join the fork to an outward handle. The handle centres start at x 333 mm and 147 mm with y 0 mm and z 75 mm above the table. Each handle is a 24 mm by 24 mm by 20 mm block. The fork slots engage the orange bar through physical contact. There is no equation that sets the output pose from the input positions. The white centre band is 8 mm wide. The green reference bar is set at 25 degrees. All joints start at zero. task.py defines every collider and joint anchor.
scoring: Any measured output carriage shift beyond 4 mm from centre makes the entire episode score zero. Any robot contact with the orange bar or the carriage also makes it score zero. Contact separation of 1 mm or less counts as contact. Otherwise score zero until the x 305 mm input moves more than positive 10 mm and the x 175 mm input moves more than negative 10 mm. Those opposing movements earn 0.25. A bar angle above 15 degrees earns 0.5. A bar angle strictly between 21 degrees and 29 degrees earns 0.75 when the carriage and both inputs each move below 4 mm per second and bar rotation is below 0.04 radians per second. Score 1.0 when both measured grippers are also open beyond 35 mm and no robot body contacts either input fork or either moving output body. Full success must hold for one second. Position history is sampled at 20 Hz. Robot contacts are checked each physics step. All other outcomes retain only the currently satisfied partial stage.
run_limit: 2400 control steps at 20 Hz. This is 120 seconds of control time.
reset_notes: Restore the fixed roots from task.py and set all four prop joints to zero. Restore the reference bars. Clear the scorer history. Nothing is consumed. Use seed 0 and object_jitter=0. Run one epoch per process.
fidelity: Rigid printed training parts with ideal guide joints. Independent articulations interact through actual fork to bar contact. No output pose or joint position is assigned during a trial. Small passive damping limits drift. A bounded zero velocity drive adds light input drag. Contact offsets are 1 mm. Guide wear and elastic bending are omitted. The stated clearances are larger than those of a precision differential.
